forecasts.label: Interest payable

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: South Oxfordshire: 67 of 131 open internal audit actions past deadline, including eight Priority 1
news_drafts.lead:
South Oxfordshire's Joint Audit and Governance Committee has been told that 67 of the 131 open actions from internal audit, the council's in-house check on whether its controls work, were past their deadlines on 25 September 2026. Eight of the 16 open Priority 1 actions, which the auditors define as fundamental to the integrity of a process, are overdue.

The report links the overdue Priority 1 actions to site visit audits at Abbey House, Cornerstone and Beacon. All three were rated Limited assurance. Together they produced 46 of the 87 actions in the 2025/26 audit plan, 19 of them Priority 1. Of the 131 open actions, 96 were raised in 2025/26 and 2026/27. Since the last update, internal audit raised 65 new actions and 105 were closed, while 51 are implemented and awaiting evidence or validation. Audits of cyber security, including artificial intelligence, and of travel and expenses were also rated Limited. The cyber audit raised nine actions, two of them Priority 1. The travel audit raised four, one of them Priority 1.

The papers report better news on other fronts. Neither South Oxfordshire nor Vale of White Horse had any external borrowing at 31 March 2026. South Oxfordshire's authorised limit, the most total debt it has told itself it will not exceed, was set at £35m. A licensing audit rated Substantial assurance, up from Satisfactory when it was last audited in May 2017. It found no discrepancies in fees tested against the 2025-26 schedule and raised only four Priority 3 actions.

Auditors also found some licence changes lacked evidence of compliance with statutory advertising requirements. None of the 39 licensing procedures reviewed had documented review dates, and some had not been reviewed since December 2020. In a separate audit, rated Substantial, five of 20 sampled report checklists (one South Oxfordshire, four Vale) lacked specialist officer sign-off on the implications sections.

news_drafts.headline: South Oxfordshire's budget surplus masks service-level overspend
news_drafts.lead: South Oxfordshire Council forecasts a £184,000 underspend for the year. But the council's own accounts show this surplus is entirely due to higher-than-expected investment income. Services across the council are forecast to overspend by £714,000. The council expects to receive £899,000 more in investment income than budgeted because interest rates have remained elevated. It holds £55m in investments. Without this extra investment income, the council would face a £714,000 overspend. The financial position is therefore dependent on the interest rate environment remaining high.

findings.headline: Council outperformed peer authorities by 0.23 per cent in treasury benchmarking
findings.detail: In the MUFG Benchmarking club peer group, South Oxfordshire outperformed the average performance by 0.23 per cent. This was achieved while maintaining a very low-risk investment profile weighted toward local authority deposits and money market funds.
findings.matters: Peer outperformance in treasury management with a lower-risk approach demonstrates above-average financial management capability relative to comparable councils.
findings.figures: 0.23 per cent above MUFG club average
findings.quote: The council outperformed the average of the group by 0.23 per cent with a very low risk profile of investments, mainly with local authorities and money market funds.

findings.headline: Investment properties income reversed from £0.681 million loss to £0.963 million profit
findings.detail: The council's portfolio of investment properties (land, depots, garages, shops) generated £0.963 million income in 2025-26, compared to a loss of £0.681 million in the prior year. The net book value of the property portfolio increased from £5.1 million to £5.7 million. Gross rate of return for 2025-26 was 17.6 per cent.
findings.matters: The swing from loss to income represents improved cash generation from the asset portfolio and increased balance sheet value.
findings.figures: £0.963 million income 2025-26; £0.681 million loss 2024-25; £5.7 million net book value 2025-26 (£5.1 million 2024-25); 17.6 per cent gross return
findings.quote: Income generated was £0.963 million in 2025/26 (£0.681 million loss in 2024/25)

findings.headline: Fixed-term deposits and liquidity instruments returned 4.82 per cent against 3.94 per cent benchmark
findings.detail: The council's treasury deposits achieved a return of 4.82 per cent compared to the 3-month SONIA benchmark of 3.94 per cent, outperforming by 0.88 percentage points. Performance was supported by active treasury management including daily balance reviews, concentrated investment during seasonal peaks such as the Christmas period when £33 million was invested, and switching to the ICD investment platform which increased money market income by 0.2 per cent.
findings.matters: Consistent outperformance of treasury benchmarks by this margin indicates skilled financial management and generates material additional returns on cash holdings.
findings.figures: 4.82 per cent actual; 3.94 per cent benchmark; 0.88 per cent outperformance; 0.2 per cent increase from platform change; £33 million invested during Christmas period
findings.quote: The performance for the year of 4.82 per cent was 0.88 per cent above the benchmark.

findings.headline: Treasury investment income £8.6 million, £1.25 million above budget
findings.detail: The council earned £8.6 million in investment income against a budget of £7.3 million. The £1.25 million outperformance was principally due to sustained higher interest rates throughout 2025-26 and higher-than-forecast cash balances, which resulted from capital spending phasing and removal of a planned office development from the capital programme.
findings.matters: Unexpected income uplift of this magnitude improves the council's financial flexibility and demonstrates effective cash management.
findings.figures: £8.6 million actual; £7.3 million budget; £1.25 million variation
findings.quote: The actual return achieved was £1.25 million more than the original budget.

findings.headline: Council switched to ICD investment platform in February 2026 with early indication of 0.2% improvement in money market income
findings.detail: Treasury moved to ICD investment platform in February, allowing daily selection from multiple money market fund providers. Early indications suggest this operational change increased money market income by 0.2%. This reflects active treasury management culture including daily balance reviews and placement of receipts up to 5pm.
findings.matters: Demonstrates continuous process improvement and treasury management discipline that supports sustained outperformance against benchmarks.
findings.figures: 0.2% estimated increase in money market income; £33m invested across two councils during Christmas holiday
findings.quote: In February the councils moved to using 'ICD', an investment platform which allows the choice from a number of money market funds each day. Early indications suggest using this platform has led to an increase in money market income of 0.2 per cent.
